questions.q: Why can an existing Conditional Access policy be extended to govern AWS sign-ins?
options: Because once AWS IAM Identity Center is federated as an Entra ID enterprise application, it is a target application Conditional Access already knows how to evaluate
Conditional Access cannot actually govern AWS; AWS requires a completely separate product
AWS automatically adopts whatever policy Microsoft 365 uses, with no configuration needed
Conditional Access only works for applications hosted physically inside Azure datacenters
questions.explain: Conditional Access evaluates sign-ins to target applications, and AWS IAM Identity Center becomes one of those target applications the moment it's set up as a federated Entra ID enterprise app — no separate access-control concept is needed.

questions.q: What is the advantage of adding the "AWS IAM Identity Center" app to an existing Conditional Access policy instead of writing a brand-new AWS-only policy?
options: New policies are always rejected by Entra ID if one already exists
It bypasses the need for MFA entirely
It only works for free-tier Entra ID licenses
One rule governs both Microsoft and AWS sign-ins, so a change like tightening MFA applies to both environments at once instead of drifting apart
questions.explain: Extending the trusted existing policy means both environments are evaluated by the identical standard and move together when the policy changes, rather than drifting apart as two independently maintained rule sets.

questions.q: Which of these is a real signal a Conditional Access policy can evaluate when deciding whether to allow a sign-in?
options: The AWS region the user plans to deploy resources into
The dollar amount of the user's current AWS bill
Device compliance reported through Intune, along with sign-in risk and named location
The number of S3 buckets the user owns
questions.explain: Conditional Access evaluates identity-and-session-level signals — device compliance, sign-in risk from Identity Protection, named locations, and MFA status — not cloud resource details like regions or bucket counts.

questions.q: Once AWS IAM Identity Center issues short-lived STS credentials after a validated SAML sign-in, what is true about subsequent AWS API calls?
options: Entra ID re-evaluates the Conditional Access policy before every individual API call
They are not individually re-checked against the Conditional Access policy; sign-in frequency settings control how often the session must be refreshed instead
AWS blocks all API calls until the Conditional Access policy is manually re-run
STS credentials are re-issued automatically every second to simulate continuous evaluation
questions.explain: AWS doesn't ask Entra ID's permission on every API call. Conditional Access's sign-in frequency setting is the practical substitute, forcing the user back through re-authentication after a defined interval.

questions.q: For a policy gating cloud infrastructure access, which combination of signals best reflects what this lesson recommends?
options: No MFA requirement, since federation alone is considered sufficient
Only a password, since AWS already encrypts traffic in transit
Only checking the user's job title in the HR system
Device compliance via Intune, phishing-resistant MFA, and sign-in risk from Identity Protection
questions.explain: The lesson recommends leaning on device compliance, phishing-resistant MFA (especially for admin-level permission sets), sign-in risk, and named locations — not weaker or unrelated signals.
